items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: So this fellow's name was Billy White, and he used to write us some arrangements.

ctx.x: arrangements. There was a fellow who was an excellent musician, played with Duke Ellington, or wrote music for Duke and everything, and later sort of came to kind of a tragic end... Because as a young man he was very brilliant; I think he graduated from Juilliard. His name was Billy White. He played with Duke briefly in the Forties, and he was the kind of a guy that could have... He was ahead of his time, really, because he could have been an excellent contract musician As a clarinet player, anyone who ever heard…

So this fellow's name was Billy White, and he used to write us some arrangements. And then listening to records, we would pick out things that the bands were playing and try to duplicate them. In the meanwhile, I would get some brilliant idea and I would sit down at the piano, and I would make a chord for somebody and tell each saxophone what to play, then I would make another one and tell the trumpets what to play, and tell the other guys, and then just hit it and see what it sounds like. Then that sounds good,…
